newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.10 pct.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday set its repo rate at an unchanged, fixed 4.10 percent.
The straight repurchase operation will run for one week from April 23 to April 30.
The Riksbank said bids had to be received by 0800 GMT on April 22 with the lowest accepted volume 200 million crowns and the highest accepted volume 15 billion crowns.
This was the second week the bank has run a straight repurchase operation, buying governmment securities and other valid securities for resale on April 30.
Previously the bank was running reverse repurchase operations where it sold securities and repurchased them a week later.
The market had not expected any change to the repo rate that was last moved on December 17 when the bank lowered the rate 25 basis points.
In 1996 the Riksbank cut the repo 25 times from a starting level of 8.91 percent to 4.10 percent.
The bank's other key interest rates, the deposit and lending rates, currently stand at 3.75 percent and 5.25 percent.
